subject: Mathematics
standard_explanation: Trigonometry studies the mathematical relationships between side lengths and angles in triangles. For any right-angled triangle with acute reference angle θ: sine(θ) = Opposite / Hypotenuse, cosine(θ) = Adjacent / Hypotenuse, and tangent(θ) = Opposite / Adjacent. These ratios enable the determination of inaccessible heights and distances without direct physical measurement.
simplified_explanation: Imagine looking up at a very tall tree or a kite in the sky! We can use a right-angled triangle like a giant measurement tool. The longest slanted side is called the Hypotenuse (like a playground slide!). By knowing just one angle, trigonometry lets us calculate how tall the tree is without climbing it!
key_points: A right triangle always has one 90-degree square corner.
The Hypotenuse is the longest side directly across from the 90-degree corner.
Sine = Opposite / Hypotenuse (how high it goes vs the long slide).
Tangent = Opposite / Adjacent (used to find building and tower heights).
examples: Calculating the height of a flagpole using its shadow length and sun angle.
An airplane measuring its glide angle to land safely on a runway.
misconceptions: Misconception: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent only work on giant triangles. Fact: The ratios depend only on the angle, regardless of how small or large the triangle is.
Misconception: The Hypotenuse can be shorter than other sides. Fact: The Hypotenuse is always strictly the longest side in a right triangle.

visual_scenes.title: Right-Angled Triangle Parts
visual_scenes.description: A clear blue right-angled triangle with square 90-degree corner, labeled Opposite, Adjacent, and Hypotenuse.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 1: The right triangle! The longest side is the Hypotenuse slide.

visual_scenes.title: Looking Up at the Angle (Theta θ)
visual_scenes.description: An observer on the ground looks upward at an angle θ toward the top of a tall green pine tree.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Looking up at angle θ! The tree is the Opposite side; ground is Adjacent.

visual_scenes.title: Calculating Height via Tangent Ratio
visual_scenes.description: The math formula shines: tan(θ) = Height / Distance. The height appears with sparkling green stars.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Math magic! Tangent lets us calculate tree height without climbing!

sign_glossary.description: Both index fingers and thumbs touch to form a complete 3-sided triangle in the air.
sign_glossary.movement: Held clearly in front of chest

sign_glossary.description: Non-dominant horizontal hand, dominant flat hand opens away from palm showing angle separation.
sign_glossary.handshape: Flat hand pivoting away from palm

sign_glossary.description: Y-handshapes tap thumbs together twice showing ruler increments.

assessment_questions.question: What is the longest side of a right-angled triangle called?
assessment_questions.hint: It is the long slanted slide opposite the 90-degree corner.

assessment_questions.question: What is the definition of Sine in a right-angled triangle?
assessment_questions.hint: Sine is Opposite divided by Hypotenuse.
